statement: Let n = len(words). Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n and for every i with 0 <= i < n the following holds. If n - 1 < k, then r[i] = 0. If n - 1 >= k, then r[i] is the maximum, over all subsets I of {0, 1, ..., n-1} such that i is not in I and |I| = k, of the common prefix length of the strings {words[j] : j in I}, where the common prefix length of a nonempty finite set S of byte strings is the largest L >= 0 such that for every p with 0 <= p < L and every s in S, p < len(s), and for all s, t in S, s[p] = t[p].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters (each byte is an ASCII code) with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(words).
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: Let M = max{len(words[j]) : 0 <= j < len(words)}. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 0 <= r[i] <= M.
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), r[i] = 0.
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words) and len(words) = k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), r[i] = max{len(words[j]) : 0 <= j < len(words) and j != i}, where the maximum over an empty set is defined to be 0.
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), r[i] is the common prefix length of the set {words[j] : 0 <= j < len(words) and j != i}, i.e. the largest L >= 0 such that for every p with 0 <= p < L and all j, j' with 0 <= j < len(words), 0 <= j' < len(words), j != i, and j' != i, we have p < len(words[j]) and words[j][p] = words[j'][p].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 2 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k = len(words) - 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i < len(words) and 0 <= j < len(words), if words[i] = words[j] (equal byte arrays), then r[i] = r[j].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: Let r1 be the result of the function on input (words, k1) and r2 the result on input (words, k2). Whenever both calls return results, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), r1[i] >= r2[i].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k1 and k2 are integers with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= len(words).

statement: Let sigma be a bijection of {0, ..., n-1} and define words_sigma by words_sigma[t] = words[sigma(t)] for 0 <= t < n. Let r = f(words, k) and r_sigma = f(words_sigma, k). Whenever both calls return results, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r_sigma[i] = r[sigma(i)].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with n = len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < n at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever both calls f(words, k) and f(words', k) return results r and r', for every i with 0 <= i < n, if the multisets {words[j] : 0 <= j < n and j != i} and {words'[j] : 0 <= j < n and j != i} are equal, then r[i] = r'[i].
preconditions: words and words' are slices of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters, both of length n >= 1, and the sum of their word lengths is at most 10^5 each; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), there exist k distinct indices j_1, ..., j_k with 0 <= j_m < len(words) and j_m != i for all m, such that the common prefix length of {words[j_1], ..., words[j_k]} equals r[i], where the common prefix length of a nonempty set S of strings is the largest L >= 0 such that for every p with 0 <= p < L and every s in S, p < len(s), and for all s, t in S, s[p] = t[p].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words) and len(words) - 1 >= k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words) and every subset I of {0, ..., len(words)-1} \ {i} with |I| = k, the common prefix length of {words[j] : j in I} is at most r[i], where the common prefix length of a nonempty set S of strings is the largest L >= 0 such that for every p with 0 <= p < L and every s in S, p < len(s), and for all s, t in S, s[p] = t[p].
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist a byte string s and a set J of indices with J subset of {0, ..., len(words)-1}, |J| >= k + 1, and words[j] = s for every j in J, then for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), r[i] >= len(s).
preconditions: words is a slice of nonempty byte strings over lowercase English letters with len(words) >= 1 and the sum of len(words[j]) over 0 <= j < len(words) at most 10^5; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(words).
